item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Aug 19, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Greenwood Lake Hike — Sun Sep 6, 10:00 AM — Meet at the Student Recreation Center
item.description:
Join us for a scenic hike along Marshall Hill Road Ruins near Greenwood Lake Airport, featuring multiple trail loops ranging from 2 to 6+ miles. Wear sturdy shoes and come ready for an adventurous day outdoors in New Jersey. How do I Sign-up?
Please register in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). Cost for Students $10
Where and When?
September 6, 2026 10am-5pm Begins Student Recreation Center
What to bring: Water, sneakers and a sense of adventure!
Potential Hazards: Unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites, and injury by running, including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.

item.title: Tech Talks — Tue Sep 8, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

item.title: Theme of the Month Book Club — Thu Sep 10, 6:30 PM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
Looking for new books to discover and fellow readers to connect with? Join Theme of the Month Book Club, a monthly gathering where participants read a book of their choice based on a shared theme and come together to discuss their selections.
Each month, a new theme will be announced—such as historical fiction, books by debut authors, found family, travel, mysteries, and more! Rather than everyone reading the same title, participants are free to choose any book that fits the theme and share their thoughts with the group.
This relaxed and welcoming book club is a great way to broaden your reading horizons, discover new recommendations, and enjoy lively conversations with other book lovers.
Themes:
September: Fresh Starts
October: Banned Books
November: Gratitude and Gathering
December: Home for the Holidays

The Mindful Stream Feel free to join as we get still and practise presence within this moment. We will discuss and observe the obstacles that, seemingly, block us from being present and bring awareness to our unconsciousness in a safe, inclusive and affirming way.
Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teaching and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous.
See you there!
Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.
Emrys has been passionate about mindfulness since 2010 and since 2021 he has been organising free, weekly online meditation groups. For more information on his free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group, visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/).
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: My Bicentennial Summer: A True-Life Adventure Across America with G. Neri — Thu Aug 20, 7:00 PM — Glen Ridge Free Public Library
item.description:
Offering a unique glimpse into the heart of America’s history - the good, the bad, and the ugly - celebrated author G. Neri invites readers for a journey through the U.S. in his funny and heartfelt book, My Bicentennial Summer.
The year is 1976, and America is throwing its biggest birthday party ever: its bicentennial. What better way to celebrate than with an eight-thousand-mile road trip? In this vibrant follow-up to his travelogue, My Antarctica, author G. Neri recalls his family’s real-life journey in a station wagon crossing twenty-six states in seven weeks, from California to Washington, DC, with only the aid of paper maps and transistor radios rather than smartphones and GPS.
Young Greg is entranced by the variety of accents, strange foods, natural wonders, and historical attractions, from the Grand Canyon to the Statue of Liberty. item.title: High Altitudes and High Stakes: A Miss Marple Mystery with Lucy Foley — Thu Aug 27, 2:00 PM — Glen Ridge Free Public Library
item.description:
Join us for a thrilling conversation with acclaimed author Lucy Foley as we delve into her brand-new Miss Marple mystery, Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel.
High in the Swiss Alps, accessible only by a single, winding railway, stands the luxurious Grand Alpine Hotel. With glorious mountain views and exclusive access to powdery slopes, it draws guests from far and wide.
The notorious actress.
The high-flying politician.
The society wife.
The reckless friend.
The shrewd doctor.
But not everyone is here for a winter holiday. Beneath the champagne and furs, dark histories simmer; old grudges emerge like cracks in the ice. And someone is watching from the shadows. A polite, unassuming woman with an extraordinary mind: Miss Marple. When a body is found and a blizzard cuts off all escape, only Miss Marple can connect the clues before the killer strikes again. Because it isn’t a question of who has a motive, but who’s next…

item.title: The Democracy We Must Keep: Why the Ideas that Built America Still Matter with David O. Stewart — Tue Sep 1, 2:00 PM — Glen Ridge Free Public Library
item.description:
Join us as we chat with award-winning historian David O. Stewart about his newest work, The Democracy We Must Keep, and the question he explores throughout the book: What did America's founders say about democracy, and can we remain true to their vision for America?
Two hundred fifty years ago, passionate men attempted to create something the world had never seen before: a nation built not on kings or armies, but on ideas where the people ruled.
In The Democracy We Must Keep, historian David O. Stewart takes readers inside the nine key documents that shaped the formation of the United States—from Patrick Henry's thunderous cry for liberty to the carefully crafted design of a government chosen by the people, with limits on all officials holding power under the Constitution.
Through the words of seven visionary founders—Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Hamilton, Gouverneur Morris, and others—Stewart shows how a fragile experiment in self-government took shape.
